findings.name: cranial nerve examination
findings.result: Bilateral facial paralysis; pupils 3 mm and reactive bilaterally.

findings.name: cerebrospinal fluid analysis
findings.result: 2 WBCs, 32 RBCs; protein 56 mg/dL; glucose 97 mg/dL (serum glucose 159 mg/dL).

findings.name: brain MRI
findings.result: Poorly marginated T2-FLAIR hyperintense foci in the left cerebral peduncle, bilateral pons and medulla, with slight T1 hypointensity and faint contrast enhancement. Diffusion-weighted imaging: restricted diffusion in the pons.

gold.reasoning: 1. Guillain–Barré syndrome was considered because of acute quadriparesis, but excluded because “The preserved reflexes, absence of sensory deficits, and brain MRI abnormalities were against the diagnosis of GBS.” 2. Multiple sclerosis was considered given multifocal CNS lesions, but deemed unlikely because “The lack of oligoclonal bands of CSF, bilateral neurologic signs, and configuration of lesions in MRI were not in line with the diagnosis of MS.” 3. Autoimmune encephalitis was considered, but excluded because “Autoimmune encephalitis has some key symptoms such as seizures, memory deficits, and psychiatric manifestations, none of which existed in this case.” 4. Cerebrovascular stroke was considered, but ruled out because “Lack of changes in the level of consciousness, gradual progression of symptoms, and clinical and imaging localization didn't match stroke.” 5. Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis was supported by the post-vaccination prodrome, multifocal poorly marginated demyelinating lesions on MRI, elevated CSF protein without oligoclonal bands, and MR spectroscopy findings.
